about: Retexture (change) test cases. Each view is rendered from a downloaded scan under data/ (git-ignored), so this file holds no pictures. `find` is the finder command that makes the case's found.json (clicks are on the 0-1000 scale of the view). `python -m edit_agent.change.suite` runs the finder, then `pans` for a case marked pans (the thing edited in up to four panoramas that see it, with a consistency sheet per case), else `one`. `group`: recolor (one colour to another), neutral (from or to white, grey, beige, black or gold, where hue says little), restyle (a new material or finish), pattern (a bold invented pattern: the cross-panorama test), form (the shape may change a little), texture (a new picture or a strong grain: the cross-panorama test). `verdict` is a person's judgement of the result after looking at the sheet, starting with good or bad; the suite compares it with the checks. `expect` is what the checks should say when the verdict is known in advance.

scans.2rPahZzW6H7: exterior of a Los Angeles apartment building, 11 panoramas, no mesh (no `pans`)

cases.name: pillows-recolor
cases.verdict: good: both teal pillows are red; their grey pattern and piping stay grey
cases.request: change the blue pillows to red
cases.find: look --scan zzvymDx5ty7 --pano 1 --yaw 213.1 --pitch -16.5 --request "change the blue pillows to red"
cases.want: Every teal-green part of the patterned pillows turns red; their grey pattern and piping stay grey; the plain cream sofa, the painting and the wall do not change. The user says blue, the photo's pillows are teal-green: the colour rule must find the pillows' own hue.
cases.panoramas: 1 (sofa, the found view), 4 and 7 also see the pillows (qwen_test sofa_pillows).
cases.notes: Plural: `look` returns all four patterned pillows in one view, as one mask. Some are mostly grey; their grey stays.
